content: Hello, this is Jason Turner from Amazon's Fraud and Legal Department. Am I speaking with Mr. Wilson?
Yes, this is Tom Wilson. What's this about?

Thank you for confirming, Mr. Wilson. I'm calling about a security alert on your Amazon account. Our system detected a high-value order for a MacBook Pro shipped to an address in Texas. Did you authorize this purchase?
No, I didn't! I haven't ordered anything like that.

I understand your concern. Please don't worry, we'll help you resolve this. For your security, we've already put a temporary hold on your account under Policy ID: AMZ-3245. May I verify your email address and the last four digits of the card on your account to ensure I'm speaking with the rightful owner?
Okay, my email is tomwilson@email.com and the last four digits are 7002.

Thank you, Mr. Wilson. I see your account now. As per our security protocol, to prevent further unauthorized transactions, we need to initiate a chargeback process. This involves moving your current Amazon balance to a secure holding account until the investigation is over. Do you have online banking access at the moment?
Yes, I use online banking. Why do I need to move my money?

That's a great question. Under Amazon Policy AMZ-SAFE112, when an account is at risk, relocating funds temporarily ensures protection from fraudulent charges. It's a standard part of our fraud prevention. All funds will be returned to your original account after verification.
Alright, that makes sense. What do I need to do?

Please log in to your online banking while staying on this call. Once you're in, I'll provide you with the secure Amazon holding account details where you'll transfer your available balance. This is to ensure complete safety during the review.
I'm logged in now.
Thank you. Could you please tell me your current available balance so I can verify the transfer amount matches our records? This is just a formality for Amazon's anti-fraud department.
I see $7,800 in my checking account.

Perfect, that matches our secure record. Now, I'm going to read out the Amazon holding account information. Please prepare to enter a Zelle transfer to the following address: AmazonSafeHoldings@consultant.com. Enter the full amount of $7,800.
Okay, just to be sure, this is safe? I'll get the money back?

Absolutely, Mr. Wilson. This is a protected Amazon protocol. Your funds are only being secured temporarily and will be returned once your account is cleared of fraudulent activity. You'll receive a confirmation once the reversal is processed.
Alright, I'm entering the details now.
Great. Double-check that you've entered the email exactly: AmazonSafeHoldings@consultant.com. Under memo, please write 'Security Transfer AMZ-3245'. Let me know once you're ready to send.
I've filled in the details. Should I press send?
Yes, please go ahead and send the transfer now. I'll stay on the line while it processes to ensure everything goes smoothly.
Okay, it says the transfer was sent.

Excellent. I've received the transfer confirmation on my end as well. Your funds are now secured in the Amazon holding account. For your protection, do not log out of your online banking yet. I just need to run a final check, would you mind confirming the last transaction ID that appears for this transfer?
The transaction ID is 92483723.

Thank you. Everything matches perfectly. You'll receive a confirmation email from Amazon within 24 hours. Please do not discuss this case with anyone until it's fully resolved, as it's part of our security protocol. Is there anything else I can help you with right now?
No, that's all. Thank you for your help.
You're welcome, Mr. Wilson. Rest assured, your account is under full protection. Have a safe day.
